audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in rialzo del 2.68%, Shanghai in rialzo dello 0.87%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura positiva per i mercati europei.

L'S&P 500 ha chiuso in rialzo dello 0.17%, il VIX è in calo dello 0.12%. Il Dollar Index è stabile, in rialzo dello 0.05% a 99.24 L'oro è in calo dello 0.29% sotto i 4530 dollari l'oncia. Il petrolio è in rialzo del 2.8% a 105.45 dollari. I rendimenti dei titoli di stato americani sono in aumento, con il US 10Y Yield in rialzo dello 0.31% al 4.58%. I BTP 10Y sono stabili al 3.73%.

L'UE ha tagliato le previsioni di crescita a causa dell'aumento dell'inflazione dovuto alla guerra in Iran. La Francia ha dichiarato che i paesi devono avere chiarezza sulla guerra prima di attingere alle riserve petrolifere. Il viaggio del premier indiano Modi in Europa ha portato a nuovi accordi tecnologici e di difesa per ridurre la dipendenza da Cina e Stati Uniti.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. 
Bitcoin si mantiene sopra i settantasettemila dollari, con una variazione del -0,81%. 
I flussi ETF hanno registrato una uscita di 70,5 milioni di dollari. 
Questo movimento potrebbe essere influenzato dalle recenti dinamiche di mercato.

Tra le altre criptovalute, Ethereum scende dello 0,58% a duemilacentoventitre dollari, 
mentre Solana guadagna lo 0,29% a ottantasei dollari e novantanove centesimi. 
BNB invece registra un aumento dello 0,73% a seicentocinquantanove dollari e dodici centesimi.

Il Fear & Greed Index è a 28, in zona Fear, 
suggerisce cautela sugli investitori.

Sui mercati attendiamo i dati economici in uscita oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani.
audio_script_en: Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing. The Nikkei closed up 2.68%, Shanghai up 0.87%, suggesting a positive opening for European markets. The S&P 500 closed up 0.17%, the VIX down 0.12%. The Dollar Index is stable, up 0.05% to 99.24 Gold is down 0.29% below $4,530 per ounce. Oil is up 2.8% to $105.45 US Treasury yields are rising, with the US 10Y Yield up 0.31% to 4.58%. The 10Y BTPs are stable at 3.73%. The EU cut growth forecasts due to rising inflation caused by the war in Iran. France stated that countries need clarity on the war before tapping into oil reserves. Indian Prime Minister Modi's trip to Europe led to new technology and defense agreements to reduce dependence on China and the US. No major macroeconomic data releases today. Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin remains above $77,000, with a change of -0.81%. ETF flows recorded an outflow of $70.5 million. This movement may be influenced by recent market dynamics. Among other cryptocurrencies, Ethereum falls 0.58% to $2,123, while Solana gains 0.29% to $86.99 BNB instead records an increase of 0.73% to $659.12 The Fear & Greed Index is at 28, in Fear zone, suggesting caution for investors. We are awaiting economic data releases today. For a deeper dive into today's topics, find the full articles in the Top Stories section on our platform. Thank you for your attention, and we'll see you tomorrow.

articles.title: Elasticity of money in production networks, working capital, credit lines and financial conditions
articles.snippet: by Ryan Niladri Banerjee, Hyun Song Shin, Jose María Vidal Pastor The elastic supply of money through overdrafts and credit lines overcomes cash-in-advance constraints, enabling large-value payments without waiting for incoming cash. This elasticity is crucial in long supply chains, where cash-in-advance constraints could otherwise cause gridlock. In essence, money elasticity and the supply of working capital are two sides of the same coin, with undrawn credit lines serving as the operative link. This paper examines how shifts in financial conditions influence money elasticity and, in turn, impact firm activity within production networks. Using granular firm-level data, we demonstrate that production-network-driven working capital needs introduce a cyclical element that dances to the tune

articles.title: Europe’s Dangerous Hunger Games for American Troops
articles.snippet: Every time reports emerge about a potential reduction of U.S. forces or capabilities in Europe, the old continent falls into the same cycle of anxiety and panic. The same applies to announcements about delayed or suspended deployments, planned rotations, or broader force posture reviews.A brief historical reminder here is necessary. The 2014 Wales Defense Investment Pledge is still often misunderstood in Europe as little more than an American demand for higher defense spending. In reality, it reflected something broader already taking shape in Washington: the expectation that Europe would gradually assume far greater responsibility for conventional defense on its own continent. The post Europe’s Dangerous Hunger Games for American Troops appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: UK Fuel Crunch Forces Starmer to Face Difficult Policy Choices
articles.snippet: Sir Keir Starmer has spelt out a number of policies to address fuel shortages, signalling the government’s fears that the Iran war could hit motorists and households. During Prime Minister’s Questions, Starmer defended an announcement last year to “phase” new sanctions on Russia, while also trailing a policy to freeze a 5p fuel duty cut beyond September. The government pledged to introduce a new sanction on oil and gas flows from Russia that passed through third countries, announcing the measure last October. …

articles.title: Why Saudi Arabia Is Losing Asia’s Oil Buyers
articles.snippet: Saudi crude exports have been falling since the US- Iran war began, but the latest slide is no longer just a story of disrupted trade routes. Cargoes scheduled to sail from Saudi Arabia in May are now assessed at roughly 3.9 million b/d (historic lows), while almost every major Saudi buyer – China, Japan, South Korea, India and Taiwan – is cutting nominations for the months ahead. China, still Saudi Aramco’s largest customer, is expected to take only about 600,000 b/d of Saudi crude in June, roughly half April’s volume.…
